transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I know people think it sounds strange, but I’m certain there are forces directing my art and that this exhibit has a special destiny, no matter what anyone says. I can feel it clear as day, even if my family doesn't understand.
Can you describe these forces you feel are directing your art, and how you know they are real?

I can feel, clear as day, that a higher power and even famous artists from the past are working right through my hands when I paint. My daughter says that's impossible, but I just know she's wrong and that this show has a special destiny. It is meant to change history and how people see my work forever, and I can't ignore that.
Do you ever hear voices or sounds that others can't, that might be related to these forces or higher powers guiding your art?

No, I don't actually hear any physical voices or sounds. It's more of a deep, absolute feeling inside me, where I can feel a higher power and famous artists from the past physically working right through my hands when I paint.
Do you believe that you are the only one who can create this kind of art, or that you have a special role or mission in the world that goes beyond just being an artist?

Yes, absolutely, I am stepping into my real role as an artist that people will study in history books someday. It's clear to me that I see things in a way nobody else on Earth does, and I have a unique mission to bring this vision to life. With a higher power and famous artists of the past working through my hands, this exhibit has a truly special destiny.
Do you think these forces or higher powers are controlling any other aspects of your life beyond your art, or is their influence mainly limited to your creative work?

No, their influence is strictly focused on my art and this upcoming exhibit. It's only when I'm painting that I feel a higher power and past artists working directly through my hands. They aren't controlling other everyday parts of my life, they are just guiding this creative work toward its special destiny.

Have you ever had any experiences or beliefs like this before, where you felt guided by a higher power or had a special mission, or is this something that started recently with your art and this exhibit?

No, I've never experienced anything like this before in my life. It only started about three months ago, right when I got into this incredibly energized, revved-up state. Before this, I never had these kinds of beliefs about invisible forces or a special destiny.

You mentioned that these beliefs started about three months ago, can you tell me more about what was happening in your life or how you were feeling right before this started, and if there was a specific event or change that might have triggered these new beliefs?

Before this started, I was dealing with a lot of joint pain and fatigue, and my wife was diagnosed with a chronic heart condition that required a lot of caregiving and doctor visits. Trying to manage all of that while pushing myself to finish my "legacy" art exhibition created this intense sense of urgency. That pressure just seemed to build up until I suddenly got into this revved-up, energized state.

You mentioned these beliefs started about three months ago, during a time of significant stress and pressure, can you tell me if these feelings of being guided by a higher power and having a special destiny have remained constant since then, or have they waxed and waned over time?

These beliefs have been incredibly strong and constant the entire three months while I've been in this highly energized state. It's only recently, since being here in the hospital and starting the medications, that these thoughts have started to fade a bit when I finally calm down. Before that, it was completely nonstop.

You mentioned that your beliefs have started to fade a bit since being in the hospital and starting medications, can you tell me more about how your thoughts and feelings about the higher power and special destiny have changed since the medication started?

Since starting the medications and calming down, those intense feelings about a higher power guiding my hands and the show's destiny have really begun to fade. I'm starting to realize those ideas were probably tied to how overcharged and revved-up I was during that high-energy period. I still care deeply about my art, but it doesn't feel like some grand, destined mission anymore.
Now that your beliefs about the higher power and special destiny are fading, do you think you would have still believed in them if you hadn't received the medication and calmed down?

No, I definitely wouldn't have believed in them if I hadn't calmed down. Those ideas about invisible forces and the exhibit's special destiny only started once I got into that revved-up state. Now that the medication is helping me settle, I can see those beliefs were tied directly to that overcharged period.
Did you ever experience any other psychotic symptoms, such as disorganized thinking or behavior, apart from these beliefs about being guided by a higher power and having a special destiny?

No, I haven't experienced anything like disorganized thinking, hearing voices, or other unusual behaviors. Apart from the intense focus on my art and the strong beliefs I already described, my mind felt clear, just extremely fast and energized.
Can you describe your mood during this three-month period when you felt guided by a higher power and had a special destiny, was it consistently elevated, irritable, or did you experience mood swings?

My mood was swinging all over the place during those three months, often jumping from feeling completely on top of the world with intense energy to being incredibly irritable. I was so amped up and wired that if my wife asked a simple question about her heart medications, I'd suddenly bark at her because any little interruption felt like it was getting in the way of what I had to do.

Did you experience a period of abnormally elevated or expansive mood, lasting at least one week, where you felt extremely happy, energetic, or irritable, and engaged in activities that had the potential for painful consequences, such as excessive spending or reckless behavior?

Yes, for the past three months I felt incredibly energetic, constantly swinging between feeling on top of the world and being highly irritable. I also spent a lot of money we didn't have on expensive canvases, lighting, and posters for the exhibit, which caused us to fall behind on our bills. I did all of this without really thinking, even though money was tight and my wife needed things for her heart condition.
Did you have any periods where you felt extremely happy or euphoric for most of the day, for at least four consecutive days, during the past three months?

Yes, for the last three months I have frequently felt "on top of the world" and absolutely bursting with energy for days on end. At the same time, I would swing into being highly irritable and snap at others if I felt they were getting in my way. This intense, high-energy state has been going on pretty much constantly for these past three months.

Did you experience a distinct period of abnormally elevated mood, where you felt extremely happy or euphoric for most of the day, nearly every day, for at least one week, or was the mood more consistently irritable and energetic throughout the three months?

Over those three months, my mood was really a mix of both. I would swing between feeling completely on top of the world with intense energy, and then suddenly getting extremely irritable and snapping at my wife or daughter if they interrupted my work or asked simple questions.

Did your periods of feeling 'on top of the world' and extremely energetic typically last for days at a time, or were they more intermittent, with your irritability being a more constant feature throughout the three months?

Actually, this high-energy, driven state has been going on constantly for the entire three months. Most days I wake up buzzing with energy and feeling on top of the world, but I easily swing into intense irritability and snap at others the moment anyone or anything seems to get in the way of my plans. So both the high energy and the irritability have been constant features during this whole time.

Can you clarify if there were any distinct periods, lasting at least one week, where you felt consistently euphoric or extremely happy, as opposed to the more mixed mood you described with both high energy and irritability?

No, I haven't had any distinct periods of just pure happiness or euphoria without the irritability. For the past three months, it has almost always been a mix of both, where I'd swing between feeling on top of the world and snapping at people because I felt so wired and amped up.
Did you ever question the reality of these forces or higher powers guiding your art during the time you were experiencing them, or did you always believe them to be completely real?

During those months, I was completely certain and never doubted the forces for a second, even when my daughter kept telling me it was impossible. But now that I've calmed down a bit on the hospital medication, I'm beginning to realize those beliefs were really just tied to that overcharged, high-energy period.

Can you confirm whether your delusional beliefs about being guided by a higher power and having a special destiny were present throughout the entire period of your elevated mood and energy, or did they emerge after the mood changes began?

Those strong beliefs about invisible forces and the exhibit's destiny only appeared once I got into that highly revved-up, nonstop state. I didn't have those ideas before my mood and energy changed, and now that I've calmed down, they are starting to fade. It seems they were completely tied to that overcharged period.
Did the intensity of your beliefs about the higher power and special destiny directly correlate with the intensity of your elevated mood and energy levels during those three months?

Yes, they absolutely went hand-in-hand. I only had those strong beliefs about the invisible forces and the special destiny during those three months when I was highly energized and revved up. Now that my energy has started to calm down, those ideas have begun to fade away.

Did you notice that your delusional beliefs about the higher power and special destiny became less intense or faded away as your mood and energy levels returned to normal, and do you think there's a direct relationship between the two?

Yes, I definitely see a direct relationship. Those strong beliefs about a higher power and the exhibit's destiny only existed while I was in that revved-up, high-energy state. Now that the medication has helped me calm down, those ideas have faded away, and I can see they were tied entirely to that overcharged period.

Can you confirm if your delusional beliefs about the higher power and special destiny were ever present when your mood was not elevated or irritable, or if they only occurred during periods of high energy or irritability?

Yes, I can confirm that those beliefs only occurred during that high-energy, irritable period. I never had any thoughts about invisible forces or a special destiny before my mood changed. Now that the medication is helping me calm down, those ideas have faded, which makes me realize they were completely tied to that overcharged phase.

Did you experience any other delusional thoughts or beliefs beyond those related to the higher power and special destiny, such as feelings of grandiosity or persecution, during the time you were in the high-energy state?

I never felt like anyone was out to get me, but I definitely had very strong beliefs about my own status as an artist. I truly believed I wasn't just a hobbyist, but a legendary artist whose work would be studied in history books because I possessed a unique vision of the world that nobody else could understand.

Can you describe how your feelings of being a legendary artist and having a unique vision of the world relate to your beliefs about the higher power guiding your art, and have these feelings changed since you started taking medication?

They were closely connected because I felt I was chosen by that higher power to create this historically important work, which made me feel like a legendary artist. Since starting the hospital medication and calming down, both those intense beliefs and my feelings of grandeur have really faded, helping me see they were just tied to that overcharged, revved-up period.

Did your feelings of grandiosity, such as believing you're a legendary artist, precede the onset of your high-energy state and delusional beliefs about the higher power, or did they emerge simultaneously with or after these other symptoms?

They all emerged at the exact same time, about three months ago, when I first entered that high-energy, revved-up state. Before I got so overcharged and busy with the exhibit, I never had those beliefs about being a legendary artist or having a higher power guide my hands. Everything just hit me all at once once that energy kicked in.

Did you experience any other symptoms like excessive spending, reckless behavior, or increased self-importance beyond your beliefs about being a legendary artist during the three months you were in the high-energy state?

Yes, during those three months, I spent money recklessly on expensive canvases, special lighting, and posters for the exhibit, even though we were tight on funds and my wife needed that money for her medical care. I also had an intense sense of self-importance, truly believing I was a unique artist whom people would study in history books because I saw the world in a way no one else could.

Can you confirm if there was a distinct period of at least one week where you felt consistently euphoric or extremely happy without significant irritability, or was your mood consistently mixed with both high energy and irritability throughout the three months?

No, there was never a week of just pure happiness without irritability. Over those three months, my mood was always a mix where I'd constantly swing between feeling on top of the world and snapping at people because I was so wired. I was just so amped up that any little interruption, like my wife asking about her pills, would make me suddenly bark at her.

Can you confirm if there was a period of at least one week where you experienced abnormally elevated or expansive mood, such as feeling extremely happy or euphoric, that was not mixed with significant irritability, and if so, how did your beliefs about the higher power and special destiny relate to this mood state?

No, there was never a time of pure happiness; my high energy was always mixed with intense irritability and snapping at others. My beliefs about a higher power and the special destiny of my art only happened during this three-month revved-up state, and they have started to fade now that the medication is helping me calm down.

Did you experience any distinct periods of abnormally elevated or expansive mood that lasted for at least one week without significant irritability, or were your mood episodes always mixed with irritability during the three months?

No, I never had a solid week of just feeling happy without the irritability. For the whole three months, my mood was always a mix where I'd feel on top of the world one minute, but then instantly snap and get highly irritated if anything got in my way. I was just too wired and amped up for it to ever be pure happiness.

Can you confirm whether there was any point during the three months where your elevated mood and energy were not accompanied by delusional beliefs about the higher power and special destiny, even if briefly?

No, there was never a time when they didn't go hand-in-hand; those beliefs and my high energy always occurred together during those three months. The thoughts about forces guiding my art only showed up once I got into that revved-up, nonstop state, and they only started to fade when I began calming down on the hospital medication. They were completely tied to that overcharged period.
